claim.public_wording: Each model or candidate SwimSignal has built or is testing to forecast sewage spills, with how it was tested and how it did against a simple reference. A score is a past result on the rows it names, not a promise about tomorrow, and none of it is a water test.
not_claimed: a measure of the water at a spot
that a candidate will pass its read
a score from inside a running test's window
that a model is safe to rely on alone

stages.live: Live: the forecast the site shows.
stages.shadow: Running test: its window is open or about to open, and nobody reads its score before the read date.
stages.scheduled: Scheduled: the window has not opened yet.
stages.lab: In the lab: tested, not good enough yet to run beside the forecast. Kept for development.

data_kinds.held_out: scored on data the model never saw while it was built
data_kinds.seen: scored on data that was used to choose or build it: a direction, not evidence
data_kinds.live: scored on SwimSignal's own live forecasts, after the outcomes were known
data_kinds.pre_window: live rows from before its test window: reported, not deciding

measures.Brier: Brier score: the mean squared gap between the chance given and what happened (1 for a spill, 0 for none). Lower is better; 0 is perfect.
measures.ECE: Calibration error (ECE): how far, on average, the chances given were from how often spills happened at those chances. Lower is better.

counted_from: a read-only copy of the state release's dipcast.duckdb

models.name: The live spill forecast
models.predicts: For each monitored storm overflow upstream of a spot, the chance that it spills on each of the next five days, from rain, how wet the ground is, the time of year and the overflow's own record. A spot's sewage spill risk adds those chances up along the river. On rivers from May to September, a second model estimates the chance a water sample would hold more than 900 E. coli per 100 ml.
models.tested: The spill model was fitted on United Utilities' overflows in 2023 and 2024 and tested on 2025: 826,725 overflow-days. The E. coli estimate was tested on 1,502 Environment Agency samples at 31 inland bathing waters, 2024 to 2026. Since 28 September 2026 every live forecast is scored afterwards against what the overflows did, at all nine companies.
models.reference: Each overflow's long-run spill rate; for the live record also "it is spilling now or spilled in the last two days" and "more than 10 mm or 5 mm of rain in two days".

results.label: 2025, United Utilities, same-day, reanalysis rain
results.note: Skill 0.33. Rain as it fell, so weather-forecast error is left out.
results.quote: SwimSignal (the model, with each overflow's own record)0.0445

results.label: E. coli over 900 on rivers and lakes, each year left out
results.note: Climatology by water type: 0.120. On lakes neither does reliably better than chance.

results.label: Live, all companies, same-day, 29 Sep to 23 Oct 2026
results.note: Skill is 1 − Brier ÷ the reference's Brier: above 0 is better than the reference.

results.label: Same rows, against "spilling now or in the last two days"
results.note: Not shown to beat persistence on the same day.

results.label: Live, all companies, one to four days ahead, against the best simple rule
results.reference_name: rain over 10 mm in two days

verdict.quote: No company passes the promise rule.
verdict.plain: It beats each overflow's long-run rate and ranks spill days well, but it is not yet shown to beat simple rules a swimmer could use. So for now it is worded as showing what the upstream monitors say, with the forecast still being tested.

models.misses: The spill model learned from United Utilities only; other companies' overflows get the same model. It does not see runoff from fields and roads, treated sewage, wildlife, or wind and mixing on a lake, and on lakes E. coli spikes are mostly not from overflows. In Thames Water's area it was worse than persistence on the same day. Welsh overflows are not in it.
models.wrong: Its chances run too high: in the live check, 29 September to 23 October 2026, same-day spills happened 0.74 times as often as forecast (95% interval 0.65 to 0.87), and 388 of 963 high warnings came true (40%). In the 2025 test, days forecast at 85% had a spill 79% of the time.

show.why: It is the forecast, worded by what it has shown. Its live score is published every day on the Accuracy page, including where it is wrong.

models.name: Regional routing (regional-v1)
models.predicts: The same daily spill chance per overflow. At eight companies it uses a model fitted on all nine companies' records with a correction for each overflow (the nine-company model's arm (b)); at United Utilities, and anywhere else, it keeps the live forecast.
models.tested: The nine-company model was trained on the Environment Agency's 2024 and 2025 records and tested on 1 January to 31 August 2026: 3,270,537 overflow-days at 13,459 overflows. The routing rule was then chosen from those same results.
models.reference: The live forecast, each overflow's past spill rate, and a flat rate per company.

results.label: Nine-company model, arm (b), all nine companies, same-day
Same, United Utilities only
results.note: 3.4% worse, interval wholly above zero: the reason United Utilities keeps the live forecast.

results.label: regional-v1 rule, all nine companies, same-day
results.note: The rows that chose the rule, with reanalysis rain: says the rule is worth a live look, not how it will do live.
results.quote: regional-v1 (v2 at eight, production at United Utilities) | 0.03633 (13.6% below production)

verdict.quote: Neither arm passes. Both fail condition 2 at United Utilities, and only there.
verdict.plain: The nine-company model was not adopted: 11% to 23% better at eight companies, 3.4% worse at United Utilities. The routing rule is a development idea tested live from 31 October.

models.misses: Chosen after seeing the results, so its seen-data gain will shrink live. United Utilities keeps the live forecast. The test is judged on SwimSignal's own polls of the companies' live feeds: a missing or stale status counts as unknown, never as a dry day.
models.wrong: On 2026 data its calibration error was 0.009 across the nine companies, against the live forecast's 0.024 (worst company: Thames, 0.0221 against 0.0401).

window.rule: Useful if its same-day Brier at the eight companies is at least 5% below the live forecast's, with the 95% interval below zero; a company more than 5% worse goes back to the live forecast. Settled before the window opened.
window.extension: Under 10,000 known overflow-days at the eight companies: one more 28-day window.

show.why: Not until the read on 28 November 2026. If it passes, a limited rollout at the eight companies is proposed in its own change.

models.name: Live spill status as an input
models.predicts: The daily spill chance per overflow, today and four days ahead, with three more inputs: whether the overflow is spilling now, its spill hours in the last 24 hours and its spill days in the last week.
models.tested: Fitted on 2024, tested on 2025 at all nine companies: 5,077,150 overflow-days with reanalysis rain, and 1,928,619 a lead with archived forecast rain. Labels from the Environment Agency's start and stop records.
models.reference: The nine-company model without the status inputs (not the live forecast), and a flat rate per company.

verdict.quote: The status input helps at every lead, 0 to 4. As stated above, nothing deploys on this.
verdict.plain: Passed all five conditions at every lead on 2025. Not deployed: it must first work on SwimSignal's own live polls, with a fallback when the status is missing.

models.misses: With every status input missing it is much worse than the model without them (0.0537 against 0.0362 same-day). About half the same-day gain comes from how the label is defined. Northumbrian gains least. Southern reports no usable live status, so the live test says nothing about it.
models.wrong: Calibration error same-day 0.003, against 0.008 for the model without status.

window.rule: Lead by lead, against the live forecast: the 95% interval wholly below zero over the nine companies, no company with 50 or more spill rows clearly worse, calibration no worse (or at most 0.02), and spills that start from dry not clearly worse.
window.extension: Too few spill rows with a known status: runs to 5 December, read on or after 7 December.

show.why: Logged beside the forecast but never shown: no page, alert or score reads it before the read.

models.name: Lead calibration, option B
models.predicts: The live forecast's daily spill chances, re-mapped by a new calibration for each lead, fitted on 2025 at the eight companies other than United Utilities.
models.tested: A 2025 replay at 3,050 overflows at the eight companies, the map fitted on odd months and scored on even ones, then the reverse. Then a check on SwimSignal's own live forecasts, 29 September to 16 October 2026: 79,084 scored forecasts, 2,334 with a spill.
models.reference: The live forecast with the map in use today.

results.label: 2025 replay, leads 0 to 4 together
results.note: No interval was worked out for the replay.
results.quote: B: production model + a map fitted on these rows, cross-fitted by month | 0.03818

results.label: Live forecasts, 29 Sep to 16 Oct 2026
results.note: Before the window: reported, not deciding.

verdict.quote: On these rows B would fail all three conditions.
verdict.plain: No verdict yet: the window decides. The live rows before it, and 2025's records, point in opposite directions.

models.misses: Fitted on 2025's records, where the forecast ran too low; on the live rows the forecast already runs too high at six of nine companies, and B raises it further.
models.wrong: On the live rows before the window its mean chance was 0.0615 against 0.0295 observed (today's map: 0.0393).

window.rule: All three: lower Brier than today's map; no company with 50 or more spills more than 2% worse; calibration error no worse. At least 200 spills.

models.how: Nothing extra is logged: at the read the map is applied to the live forecast's own published scored rows.

show.why: Nothing is deployed unless all three conditions hold at the read.

models.name: Company calibration (A8)
models.predicts: The live forecast's daily spill chances with a frozen correction for each overflow at the eight companies other than United Utilities, fitted on SwimSignal's own polls.
models.tested: Fitted on 20,783 same-day rows, target days 29 September to 23 October 2026, 1,010 overflows. No score was worked out on the fitting rows. The corrections are frozen in a file with a SHA-256 beginning 2662dcfa.
models.reference: The live forecast and a flat rate per company.

verdict.plain: Not yet run. The prediction written before the window was that it will not be adopted.

models.misses: Overflows that never spilled get corrections only down to 0.73 of the forecast, not lower. United Utilities is not changed.
models.wrong: Background, before the window: the live forecast's Brier over the eight companies was about 9% above a flat rate's (Thames about 57%, Southern 41%, Wessex 23%).

window.rule: Shown better than both the live forecast and the flat rate over the eight companies (95% interval wholly below zero), and no changed company clearly worse.
window.extension: Too few spills at a changed company: 14 days more, to 6 December, read on or after 9 December.

models.how: Nothing extra is logged: at the read the frozen corrections are applied to the live forecast's own published scored rows.

show.why: Never deployed before the read, and only then if the conditions hold.

models.name: Ensemble rain (D4)
models.predicts: The spill forecast run on each of three members of the Met Office's MOGREPS-UK ensemble rain forecast, giving a range around the headline chance two to four days ahead.
models.tested: Not tested on past data: Open-Meteo does not keep the ensemble's past runs, so a backtest is not possible. The live window is the first test.
models.reference: The single rain forecast the headline uses now.
models.misses: Three members are a narrow sample of the weather. Before the window, the headline sat inside the members' range on about 70% of rows two days ahead and 65% four days ahead.

window.rule: Whether a wider range marks a larger error, and whether the members' mean is no worse than the single forecast, overall and at each lead and company.
window.extension: Too few spill rows: runs to 3 December, read on or after 5 December.

show.why: The range is shown, labelled as under test; the level and the headline chance do not use it.

models.name: Upgraded overflows, option B
models.predicts: The daily spill chance with each overflow's own correction fitted only on its record after a start date, so an overflow that was upgraded and went quiet is not judged on its old spills.
models.tested: Not yet scored. Two windows are fixed: the Environment Agency's records for 1 January to 31 August 2026, same-day; and SwimSignal's own live forecasts for target days 29 September to 30 November 2026, leads 0 to 4.
models.reference: The live forecast, and the same correction fitted on the whole record (B0).
models.misses: A broken monitor that reports no spills with fresh time stamps passes the dead-monitor check. The 16 Ilkley overflows are left out. The live window is autumn, when the forecast has run too high.

window.rule: Seven conditions, all needed, including a gain on the 2026 records with the interval below zero, no loss over 1% in the live window, and no company clearly worse.

models.how: Nothing extra is logged: at the read the arms are rebuilt from the live forecast's logged raw chances.

show.why: Not before the read. A pass leads to a separate running test early in 2027, not straight to the forecast.

models.name: Winter recalibration
models.predicts: The live forecast's chances with a fixed correction after the lead map, by lead and possibly by company, fitted on the live autumn rows to bring the chances down where they run too high.
models.tested: An earlier correction on 12 days of live rows (58,274 rows) was 4.3% better against a 5% bar. A later check on 117,324 live rows, 29 September to 23 October, found the chances run too high overall. The new correction is fitted on or after 10 December to target days 29 September to 6 December.

results.label: Earlier correction, company intercepts, 12 days of live rows
results.note: Scored leaving one day out at a time; no interval.

verdict.plain: The earlier correction missed its 5% bar. The winter test is its successor, with a different route written down before any of its rows.

models.misses: Fitted on autumn, judged on winter: whether the same bias holds in summer is not tested.
models.wrong: In the live check, of same-day forecasts in the highest band, 388 of 963 came true (40%).

window.rule: At least 1% better with the interval above zero, or no more than 1% worse with a shown calibration gain; no company clearly worse.
window.extension: If too few spills: 16 weeks, to 4 April 2027, read on or after 6 April.

models.how: Logs a separate corrected chance from the fit, never shown before its rollout review.

show.why: Not before the read. It stays a labelled secondary for 2027 and never replaces the frozen 2027 evaluation's predictions.

models.name: Spill duration
models.predicts: For an overflow spilling now, the chance it is still spilling 1, 3, 6, 12 and 24 hours later. When a spill ends is not when the water clears.
models.tested: Trained on 2024 and scored on 2025: 1,582,953 hours of spills at the nine companies. Then a replay of 2024-25 at the times SwimSignal actually polls, and a check of the 2024-25 table on SwimSignal's own polls, 28 September to 31 October 2026.
models.reference: B1: the share of a company's spills still running after the same elapsed time.

results.label: 2025, all horizons
results.note: 11.6% better, but its chances were unreliable.

results.label: 2024-25 replay at the live poll times, calibrated
results.note: Development on seen data: a direction, not a verdict.

verdict.quote: Verdict: the gate fails. Nothing was downloaded and nothing was scored on 2026
verdict.plain: The model failed its reliability condition on 2025, and the calibration gate that followed also failed. The 2024-25 table is shown as a record, not a forecast.

models.misses: It under-forecasts at 24 hours. On the live polls the 2024-25 table's curve was too flat for autumn 2026: too low at 1 hour, too high at 12 to 24 hours.
models.wrong: On 2025 its reliability failed in 24 of the 45 company-and-horizon cells. In the replay, 19.4% of rows were spills that had already stopped.

milestones.what: the same check of the table on November's polls
refit the table on three months of live polls, then a held-out month

show.why: No forecast of when a spill ends is shown. The 2024-25 durations are shown as a record of the past on the spill durations page.

models.name: The 2027 evaluation
models.predicts: Not a new model: the live forecast, frozen before the season, scored once over the whole 2027 season. Four results: spill forecasts same-day and one to four days ahead, and the E. coli estimate on rivers same-day and ahead.
models.tested: Target days 1 May to 30 September 2027, at the 1,089 overflows that reach the 105 listed spots, and about 340 river samples.
models.reference: Each overflow's spill rate adjusted for the month; each bathing water's own share of samples over 900.
models.misses: Each result shows skill only if the lower end of its 95% interval is above 0. Candidates are reported separately and never replace the frozen model's result.

milestones.what: the model is frozen and tagged before the season
the analysis runs once, on that day's snapshot

show.why: No result until the analysis runs after the season. A trial run on autumn 2026 rows checked the code; it is not a result.
